To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the latent correlation-based multiview learning and SSL paradigms are not identifiable, i.e., the learned embeddings are not unique; 2) this non-identifiability can be resolved by enforcing additional constraints on embeddings that are consistent with the underlying data generation process; 3) the resulting constrained embedding is unique and is consistent with the data distribution, and thus is a better proxy for the data manifold than the unconstrained one.

(i) the latent representations learned via multiview analysis and self-supervision can be understood from a unified identifiability perspective; (ii) the identifiability analysis of the latent representations learned by SSL algorithms can be used to understand and explain their effectiveness; (iii) the identifiablity analysis of SSL algorithms can be leveraged to improve their performance

(1) the identifiability of latent correlation-based multiview learning (e.g., (D)CCA) is determined by the correlation matrix of the views and the correlation of the labels (when available), and (2) SSL methods such as BYOL and Barlows are identifiable only if the correlation matrix of their augmented views is non-singular, i.e., the augmentation is not redundant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the theoretical understanding of the latent correlation-based multiview learning and SSL paradigms.
the theoretical understanding of correlation-based multiview learning.
the identifiability of latent correlation-based multiview learning and SSL, and its implications on representation learning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the correlation-based multiview learning (MVL) and SSL paradigms are effective, but the reasons for such effectiveness are unclear.
the correlation-based learning of neural embeddings is a powerful approach, which is effective in a broad spectrum of applications, but the theoretical foundations are still missing.
the latent correlation-based multiview learning and SSL are not identifiable, which is a major limitation of these approaches.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the correlation-based learning paradigm is not only useful for SSL but is also applicable to multiview learning, and vice versa.
